rationale.conceptual: The core method is gradient-boosted regression with Voronoi tessellation features—a documented, multi-component approach from materials informatics. It requires careful implementation of RFECV, feature generation via matminer, and model evaluation, but no novel algorithms. The difficulty lies in correctly applying existing techniques to a specific dataset and extracting meaningful feature importance rankings.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has 6 steps (data acquisition, feature generation, RFECV, model training, evaluation, and output) with dependencies between stages. Data assembly from the Materials Project and CMR can be fragile, and computing 271 Voronoi features per material across 2,398 compounds is computationally heavy. Multiple load-bearing handoffs (features → selection → model) increase orchestration complexity.
